question: What secret did you keep from your parents for years?
story: For three years my parents thought I was on the honor roll, because I was intercepting my own report cards from the mailbox. It started in seventh grade with one bad math grade I did not want to explain. I got to the mailbox first, hid the envelope, and told them the school had gone paperless. They believed me instantly, which honestly felt insulting. So I kept doing it. Every semester, same routine. I even started praising the school district for going green. Then came parent teacher night. I told them it was canceled. They showed up anyway with a pie. My mother sat down across from my math teacher, smiled, and asked how her honor roll student was doing. The room went silent. Here is the twist. My grades had actually climbed all the way to A's by then. I had been hiding proof that I was doing great. My mom still brings up that pie.
